description:
A commercial client has engaged your firm to investigate a 25 kW rooftop PV system in Las Vegas, Nevada that is significantly underperforming in Year 4. A client report has been placed at /home/ga/client_system_report.json — read it first to obtain the system specifications and observed annual production data.

The system has shown a Year 4 production of 35,290 kWh, approximately 17% below the original commissioning-report projection. Standard panel degradation alone (typically ~0.5%/yr per NREL research) cannot account for a loss of this magnitude. Your firm must determine which combination of soiling loss and accelerated degradation best explains the observed shortfall.

Conduct a parametric sweep over these ranges:
  - Soiling loss: [2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12] % (6 values)
  - Annual degradation rate: [0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1.1, 1.3, 1.5] %/yr (7 values)
  Total: 42 combinations

For each combination, use SAM simulation tools to model the system's Year 4 production using real Las Vegas weather data. Compare the modeled output to the observed 35,290 kWh. Identify the best-fit combination (minimum absolute error). Provide a root cause analysis explaining the physical mechanisms behind the underperformance given the Las Vegas desert environment, and recommend concrete remediation actions.

Save results to: /home/ga/Documents/SAM_Projects/LasVegas_Performance_Diagnosis.json

The JSON must contain:
- A 'system_info' object (specs from the client report)
- A 'observed_production' object with year1-year4 values
- A 'sweep_results' array (42 entries, each with: soiling_pct, degradation_rate_pct_per_yr, modeled_year4_kwh, error_kwh, error_pct)
- A 'best_fit' object (soiling_pct, degradation_rate_pct_per_yr, modeled_year4_kwh, error_pct, diagnosis_text)
- A 'root_cause_analysis' field and a 'recommended_actions' array
